newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent up in thin mkt on Iran-Europe tension.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent up in thin mkt on Iran-Europe tension.

text.p: SIMEX Brent prices rose in a thin market late on Friday as the market remained nervous about the ongoing tension between Iran and Europe, brokers said.
May last traded at $18.01 per barrel, up eight cents from the previous close after recording only 13 lots.
June last traded at $18.19, up five cents aftar trading three lots.
Brokers said the market was dominated by spread trading as players rolled over their May positions into June ahead of Tuesday's expiry.

Iran stepped up its attacks on Friday against a German court ruling which accused Tehran of ordering the murders of dissidents in Berlin, branding it a political show without legal value as it claimed the court had failed to follow accepted legal procedures.
The US applauded the German court finding, seeing it as a victory in its effort to persuade Europe to take a tougher line with Iran.
NYMEX ACCESS after-hours trading system last traded at $19.58, up one cent. -- Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3084)
